topic: Visit of Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan to Sri Lanka

subtopics.title: Bilateral Ties and Cooperation Areas
subtopics.summary: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan made the first-ever bilateral visit to Sri Lanka and held talks with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo. The visit highlighted trade, development, defence and development-linked cooperation between India and Sri Lanka. India is Sri Lanka's largest trade partner and largest source of tourists.

subtopics.title: Diaspora Schemes: PIO and OCI
subtopics.summary: The OCI scheme was introduced in 2005 through an amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955, and was merged with the PIO scheme in 2015. PIO card holders need no visa to visit India for 15 years from the date of issue of the card. OCI holders get a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa and are exempt from police reporting.
facts: OCI scheme introduced in 2005 via amendment to the Citizenship Act, 1955

PIO: a foreign citizen, except nationals of Pakistan, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, China, Iran, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Nepal
PIO: a parent, grandparent or great-grandparent was born in and a permanent resident of India, or the person is a spouse of an Indian citizen or PIO
PIO card holders need no visa for 15 years from the date of issue of the card
PIO stay up to 180 days is exempt from FRRO/FRO registration; longer stays must register within 30 days
OCI eligibility covers persons eligible for Indian citizenship on 26.01.1950 and their minor children
Persons who were ever citizens of Pakistan or Bangladesh are not eligible for OCI
OCI holders get a multipurpose, multiple-entry, lifelong visa and are exempt from police reporting
OCI holders have no right to acquire agricultural or plantation properties

subtopics.title: Katchatheevu Island Dispute
subtopics.summary: Katchatheevu is an uninhabited 285-acre island in the Palk Strait, and its ownership remained disputed until 1974. Sri Lanka based its claim on early medieval rule and Portuguese jurisdiction, while India's claim traced control through the Ramnad Zamindari under the Nayak dynasty of Madurai. Tensions over Indian fishermen after the 2009 Sri Lanka Civil War have renewed demands over the island.
facts: Katchatheevu is an uninhabited 285-acre island located in the Palk Strait
The island was once part of the Madras Presidency
Ownership remained a point of dispute between India and Sri Lanka until 1974
Sri Lanka's claim: Jaffna Kingdom ruled the island in the early medieval period
Sri Lanka's claim: Portuguese (1505-1658 CE) exercised jurisdiction over the islet
India's claim: control later shifted to the Ramnad Zamindari under the Nayak dynasty of Madurai in the 17th century
Indo-Sri Lankan Maritime Agreement 1974, under Indira Gandhi, agreed to cede the island to Sri Lanka
The 1974 agreement allowed Indian fishermen continued access to Katchatheevu
Additional Agreement of 1976 barred fishing by both countries in each other's EEZ, with the island at the boundary
After the 2009 Sri Lanka Civil War, arrests and torture allegations of Indian fishermen renewed Katchatheevu demands

subtopics.title: Sri Lanka Profile and Strategic Context
subtopics.summary: Colombo is the executive capital of Sri Lanka and Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte houses the legislature, with Harini Amarasuriya as Prime Minister and Anura Kumara Dissanayake as President. The LTTE, formed in 1976, and the 13th Amendment shape Sri Lanka's internal politics. China's growing presence through financial aid and Hambantota Port raises strategic concerns for India.

quizzes.passage: Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan made the first-ever bilateral visit to Sri Lanka and held talks with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in Colombo. The visit highlighted several areas where India and Sri Lanka work together. India has been Sri Lanka's largest trade partner and largest source of tourists, and the two countries share a free trade agreement that governs much of their commercial relationship. Cooperation also extends to development projects, including the construction of a solar power plant at Sampur in Sri Lanka. Defence ties are expressed through joint exercises between the armed forces, such as SLINEX, MITRA SHAKTI and MILAN. The visit also brought the Overseas Citizen of India scheme into focus. During this period Sri Lanka joined the International Big Cat Alliance. The two neighbours are separated by the Palk Strait, and the uninhabited island of Katchatheevu lies in that strait. Regional forums such as BIMSTEC and SAARC also feature in the India-Sri Lanka relationship. Sri Lanka's President is Anura Kumara Dissanayake, while its Prime Minister is Harini Amarasuriya. Together, trade, development, defence, diaspora and regional cooperation form the main dimensions of the bilateral relationship discussed during the visit.

quizzes.passage: Katchatheevu is a small island located in the Palk Strait between India and Sri Lanka. The island is uninhabited, yet its ownership remained a point of dispute between the two countries for a long time. Sri Lanka's claim rests on history, since the island was initially ruled by a kingdom of Sri Lanka in the early medieval period. Sri Lanka also argues that a European power which occupied the island for over a century exercised jurisdiction over the islet. India's claim, on the other hand, holds that control of the island later passed to a zamindari, which functioned under a ruling dynasty based in the southern part of the country. Over the years, maritime agreements tried to settle the dispute and strengthen ties. One agreement allowed Indian fishermen continued access to the island, and a later additional agreement prevented both countries from fishing in each other's exclusive economic zones. After the civil war in Sri Lanka ended, tensions rose over Indian fishermen in Sri Lankan waters, leading to arrests, torture allegations and renewed demands over the island.
